title: Velocity Labyrinth: Throughput Prober for Token Velocity and p95 Regression Detection
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Build a durable, extensible microbenchmark harness that measures tokens-per-second under realistic burst-to-sustained transitions and tracks p95 latency regressions for core serving models. The harness ("Velocity Labyrinth") expands existing TPS probes by adding: burst->steady ramps, KV warmup modes, variable context-length fixtures, deterministic replay of sampled production traces, and automated regression detection with CI gating and alerting. Deliverables: (1) a portable benchmark runner (Go + gRPC client) that can run locally or as k8s Jobs; (2) a telemetry pipeline that emits per-batch tokens/sec and per-request p50/p95/p99 with trace IDs; (3) a regression detector service that consumes historical windows and raises actionable alerts with suggested bisect ranges; (4) CI integration and a canary job in the runtime repo.
updates: 2026-03-01: Spike completed. Prototype runner implemented in Go using gRPC streaming to emulate real client patterns (open PR with prototype harness).
2026-03-03: Added KV-warmup driver to prototype; validated on small model suite (l2-small, l2-medium). Observed 8-12% cold->warm delta, matching production traces.

2026-03-05: Integrated context-length fixtures (32/256/1024) and measured impact on batch sizing heuristics. Found p95 increases at 1024 for request-constrained profiles; logged findings in Confluence.
2026-03-07: Implemented basic regression detector (moving-window comparison + bootstrapped p95 diff). Wired alerts to #runtime-sla Slack channel; still tuning false positive rate.
2026-03-09: Opened PR for k8s Job adapter (github.com/redwood-inference/bench/pull/4123). CI job currently gated by infra quota; infra team looped in for quota bump.

2026-03-10: Design review with Runtime and Observability teams. Agreed to expose per-token emission metrics and sample traces for debug. Action: add trace redaction to avoid PII before storing replay samples.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark runner can reproduce a burst->steady transition scenario end-to-end on CI and k8s (burst=2000 tps for 30s -> steady=400 tps for 10m).
Telemetry pipeline emits tokens/sec and request p50/p95/p99 with trace IDs to the experimentation metrics cluster (statsd/OTLP).
Regression detector raises alerts when p95 regresses by >10% for three consecutive windows and posts a summary with suggested bisect intervals to the ticket and Slack channel.
Two core models (l2-medium, l2-large-quant) have baseline benchmark runs stored and visible on the performance dashboard; comparisons are reproducible via CLI command.
CI integration: a lightweight canary runs on every runtime changeset; regressions fail the canary step and create a regression ticket with attached artifacts (raw traces, config).
risks: Infra quotas prevent reliable CI scheduling of k8s jobs — mitigation: fall back to a smaller-local runner and async upload of telemetry.
Noisy p95 signals from environment variance — mitigation: use bootstrapped diff, compare against multiple historical windows and require sustained deviation.
Potential leak of sensitive prompt data in replay traces — mitigation: implement redaction/hashing heuristics and review with privacy team before storing.
False positives in automated bisect suggestions — mitigation: surface confidence intervals and require manual confirmation for high-effort rollbacks.
notes: Design tradeoff: use Go runner for parity with other bench tooling (low-latency native gRPC) vs Python for flexibility. Chose Go for performance and easier containerization.
We will reuse existing tokenization fixtures from ENG-5931 to ensure consistent token counts across models.
Regression detector algorithm: start with nonparametric bootstrap of p95 differences; iterate to a Bayesian delta if false positives remain high.
Next steps: secure infra quota, finish PR review (runtime + observability), add trace redaction, add per-route config support and run baseline on dedicated pool.
